answer: A genuine usage signal from peers raises an agent's trust tier, while new identities stay quarantined in a cold inlet until they earn history. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and solve a per-epoch proof-of-work tied to its identity, so spawning many fake identities costs real compute and locked capital per sybil. Only participants past that threshold may harbor delegated voting weight, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0164's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
